name: Leave a hazard zone
summary: On a key, the unit covers a patch of ground with something that harms (fire, gas, radiation, an energy storm) or hampers (a field that slows movement and attacks). The zone forms around the unit itself, where a thrown canister lands, or at a spot picked at range, and it lasts a set time or for as long as the unit keeps feeding it. Whoever stays inside keeps taking damage or stays slowed, so its real job is denying ground: enemies must leave, go round, or pay to rush through. Many versions hurt their own side too. It is the ability home of the zone weapon trait: a weapon that leaves a zone with every shot uses the trait instead.
counterplay: Step out or go round: the zone is fixed to the ground and shows its edge, so leaving it ends the harm.
Punish the caster while it feeds the zone: planted or dousing casters can't move or fire (the Desolator, the Toxin Tractor), so out-range them or flank them.
Spread out: zones punish packed groups far more than one runner.
Send what the zone barely hurts: aircraft above it, heavy armour that wears down only slowly, or machines immune to its damage type.
Bait it out, then push while it is on cooldown.
Kill or pressure the caster first; StarCraft II players hunt High Templar before they can cast.

other_examples.note: A spell cast on a spot at range: an energy storm keeps hurting every unit in a wide circle for several seconds. Several storms on one spot do not add up. It wrecks clumped armies, so the caster becomes a target the enemy tries to kill first, and it pairs with spells that pin or slow enemies inside it.

sources.title: Psionic Storm, Liquipedia StarCraft II Wiki

other_examples.note: A slowing field: the target circle is shown on the map, switches on after a short delay, then makes enemy units and buildings inside it move and attack far more slowly for several seconds. It deals no damage, leaves friendly units alone and does not stack; players use it to stop enemies escaping or kiting.

sources.title: Time Warp, Liquipedia StarCraft II Wiki
sources.version: Legacy of the Void (patch 4.11 and later)

other_examples.note: An order on a target point: the tractor drives there and keeps dousing the ground with toxin until told otherwise, and cannot attack meanwhile. Infantry can hardly cross the soaked ground and vehicles slowly lose health in it, which the wiki suggests for sealing back routes against saboteurs.
Thrown at a ground spot, it leaves a pool of burning fuel that keeps hurting infantry standing in it. It costs munitions, needs an upgrade bought at the headquarters and has a cooldown.

sources.title: Conscript Infantry Squad, Company of Heroes Wiki
sources.note: Read from the copy-check page cache (copy fetched 2026-10-19).

shooter_analogues.note: A thrown orb bursts on the floor into a patch of crystals; anyone who crosses it is slowed, dashes and jumps included, and makes noise while moving, until the patch fades a few seconds later. It hampers rather than hurts, and it affects her own team too.

shooter_analogues.unit: Caustic: Nox Gas Trap and Nox Gas Grenade
shooter_analogues.note: Canisters he sets down ahead of time vent damaging gas once an enemy comes close or shoots them, and his ultimate throws a grenade that fills a large area with the same gas; his passive highlights enemies standing in it.

player_translation.summary: A key that turns a patch of ground into no-go territory for a while: the player floods the ground around themselves, or throws or fires the hazard at a spot, and enemies who stay in it take damage or are slowed. It wins fights by moving enemies rather than by killing them on the spot.
as_user: Read where the enemy has to walk (a choke, a capture point, the lane behind a retreating tank) and cover it; the zone works while you shoot, reposition or hold.
Planted version, as on the source unit: you root yourself and flood the ground around you, becoming a fortress against infantry, but you give up moving and your gun while planted.
Thrown version: lob a canister or orb to a point within reach, then fight from cover while it burns.
The skill is timing and placement: drop it on a push, an objective or a revive, never on empty ground, because a wasted zone means a long wait.
as_target: A coloured ground patch with a sharp rim and a hiss or crackle shows the zone before it has hurt you much: step out, go round, or rush through if the prize is worth it.
If you must cross, cross fast and spread out; a zone punishes a group far more than a single runner.
Look for the caster: a planted one cannot move, so out-range it, flank it, or send something the zone barely touches (heavy armour, aircraft, immune machines).
A slowing field does not hurt by itself, but it makes you easy prey for the caster's team, so leave it before you trade shots.
teammates: Allies keep enemies inside: a stun, a pull or suppression right after it lands turns the zone into a kill box.
Versions that hurt allies make the team plan around them: they must give way at the choke you flood, or the zone is tuned to spare friends.
On defence, a zone buys teammates time to repair, revive or fall back behind it.
The enemy team answers with counter-picks: armour or machines the zone barely hurts, long-range fire on a planted caster, or a scout that spots the caster before the field goes up.
controls: Q uses the zone. Planted version: press to root and flood the ground around you, press again to pack up (a deploy). Thrown version: hold Q to show the landing circle under the cursor, release to throw.
Left mouse stays the primary weapon; in the planted version it is locked while you are rooted.
The ground preview is the only targeting aid, so no other key is needed.
feedback: A strongly coloured ground patch with a crisp rim, drawn under units but above terrain and readable from the top-down camera at any zoom; the colour tells what it does (green toxic, orange fire, blue slow).
Strength shown by density or pulse speed, visibly thinning as it runs out.
One ambient sound per hazard type, and a tick sound with a red screen-edge flash for a player taking damage inside.
Active zones of both teams appear on the minimap as tinted circles.
A zone that also hurts allies shows an extra warning stripe to them.
changes_from_rts: RTS zones are fed by units that sit still for minutes; a player-controlled unit needs a duration and a cooldown, or one zone owns a lane all match.
RTS units walk into zones on their own; human players walk round them, so the zone must matter in the few seconds people really stand in one, and its main value is denial.
The Desolator's radiation hurts his own side as much as the enemy; in a team shooter that griefs teammates, so default to little or no harm to allies and keep full friendly fire for a spicy variant.

Infantry-first harm (radiation that kills soldiers at once but wears tanks down only slowly, or a Molotov that burns only infantry) makes a clean counter-pick and can stay, but the zone should still slow or chip vehicles a little so it is not dead weight against them.
The zone's exact edge must show from above, because players cannot hover a cursor over it as in an RTS.
In Red Alert 2, kills made by the field earn the Desolator nothing; here zone kills should credit the owner, so good placement is rewarded.

team_play.notes: The zone decides where both teams fight: allies hold enemies in it with stuns and pulls, a planted caster needs bodyguards against aircraft and armour, and the enemy team must bring units the zone barely hurts.

notes: A ground area on a timer that applies damage or a slow to everything inside is a standard shooter system built on trigger volumes.
Needs per-tick kill credit, immunity flags (machines immune to radiation) and a rule for overlapping zones: stack or not.
Ground decals must sit under units yet stay readable, and every player must see the same edge, so the zone's area is decided on the server.
The planted version reuses the deploy-mode system.
A zone on an objective can lock a point down for a long time; cap duration and size so one zone never covers a whole capture area.
Stacking zones (Red Alert 2 Desolator fields add up) can make a choke impassable; decide whether overlapping zones stack.
A planted zone on a tough unit becomes a fortress infantry cannot approach; pair it with a hard counter such as aircraft or armour.
A slow on top of damage drifts toward hard control with no escape; keep the slow moderate.
Many overlapping coloured patches in a big fight become noise; limit live zones per player and give each hazard type one clear colour.
Players must tell friendly from enemy zones at a glance, and know whether a friendly one hurts them.
The edge must be exact: damage that starts outside the drawn rim feels unfair.

variants.name: Planted field
variants.summary: Root yourself to flood the ground around you; the field stays strong while you stay put and fades slowly after you move or die. You cannot fire while planted.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Desolator (deploy); Generals Toxin Tractor (Contaminate, which stops it attacking)

variants.name: Thrown pool
variants.summary: Throw or fire a canister at a spot within reach; it bursts into a burning or toxic pool that lasts a few seconds.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes 2 Conscripts' Molotov; Apex Legends Caustic's gas grenade

variants.name: Slow field
variants.summary: The zone hurts no one but slows the movement and attacks of enemies inside, so the team can catch or out-shoot them.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Mothership Time Warp; Valorant Sage's Slow Orb

counters.why: Fast units that kite or run lose their edge while slowed inside the field.

countered_by.why: Long-range weapons hit the caster from outside the field.

variants.name: Storm at range
variants.summary: Pick a spot at range; a storm hurts every unit inside it, ground and air, friend and foe (not buildings), for a few seconds. Storms on the same spot do not stack.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II High Templar Psionic Storm

countered_by.why: Long-range weapons hit the caster from well outside its zone.
Heavy armour shrugs off most zone damage long enough to cross it or to reach the caster.

variants.name: Trap canisters
variants.summary: Set down a few visible canisters ahead of time; each vents its gas when an enemy comes close or shoots it. Unlike a mine it is in plain sight and makes a zone, not a single blast.
variants.seen_in: Apex Legends Caustic's Nox Gas Trap

variants.name: Indiscriminate
variants.summary: Full friendly fire: the zone hurts your own team exactly as much as the enemy, and is stronger or larger to make up for it.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Desolator (his own side's soldiers die in the field too)

adds_weaknesses.why: The zone is fixed to the ground and shows its edge, so alert enemies simply walk round it; its value depends on placement.
Its zone hurts teammates as much as enemies, so allies must give way wherever it is laid.

variants.name: Stacking fields
variants.summary: Zones from several players overlap and add up, so a team of the same unit can make ground impassable.

adds_strengths.why: Denies ground: enemies must leave the zone, go round it or pay to cross.

adds_weaknesses.why: The zone is fixed to the ground and shows its edge, so alert enemies simply walk round it; its value depends on placement.

counters.why: Soldiers cross a zone slowly and wear down fast inside it.
Slow units cannot get out of a zone before it has done its work.

countered_by.why: Ground zones do not reach fliers, which can strike the caster from above.
Long-range weapons hit the caster from well outside its zone.
Heavy armour shrugs off most zone damage long enough to cross it or to reach the caster.

open_questions: Should zones hurt teammates? (Recommended: little or none by default; full friendly fire only in the indiscriminate variant.)
Do overlapping zones from several players stack? Red Alert 2 Desolator fields do; StarCraft II storms do not.
Should kills made by a zone credit its owner? Red Alert 2 gives the Desolator nothing for them. (Recommended: yes.)
May a zone hurt only infantry, like the Conscripts' Molotov, or must every zone do something to vehicles too?

shooter_fit.reason: Denial zones (molotovs, gas, slow fields) are a staple of team shooters, read well from above as ground patches, reward placement and create clear counter-picks.
